gloss: What this row's subject is, in a sentence or two, for a reader who does not already know it.
use_when: The row names a thing (a view, an object, a fund, a doc, a tool) and a reader meeting it has to be told what it is before anything else is useful.
instead_of: blurb, description, desc, summary, detail, what, role, subject, short, becomes

gloss: Authored prose meant to be read as prose: several sentences making an argument or telling the row's story.
use_when: The text would survive being lifted out of the table and read on its own. A gloss that has grown past three sentences and acquired a point is a narrative.
instead_of: body, prose, copy, lede, essay, assessment, discussion

gloss: Text the row exists to carry, rather than text about something else the row holds.
use_when: The row's value IS the text and nothing in it describes a neighbouring field: a prompt to send, a template to fill, a message body. Every other name here annotates a subject; this one is the subject.

gloss: Why this row's judgment or choice was made, as against the alternative.
use_when: The row records a decision somebody could have made differently: a mapping, an override, an exclusion, a classification, a freeze, a test worth writing.
instead_of: why, reason, basis, premise, justification, argument, protects, browse_reason, mapping, unlocks

gloss: When to reach for this row's subject rather than its neighbour.
use_when: The row is one of a set a reader has to choose among, and knowing what each IS does not tell them which to pick.

gloss: What this row's subject covers, and what it deliberately does not.
use_when: Coverage is the fact a reader needs: which files a registry claims, which cases a mechanism reaches, what a check actually holds.
instead_of: reaches, renders, covers, applies_to, extent, where, recognizes

gloss: The measured check behind the row, with the figures in it.
use_when: There is a number, a count, or a reconciliation a reader could re-run. Evidence cites; rationale argues; upkeep says who keeps it true.
instead_of: verify_seam, concordance, coverage, shows, finding, proof, measurement

gloss: What limits, qualifies, or complicates the row, said where the row is read.
use_when: A reader who took the row at face value would be wrong in some specific and nameable way.
instead_of: comparison_basis, assumptions, wellformedness, implication, limit, warning, gotcha, boundary, misses, declines_to

gloss: Where this row's content came from, and how it would be reproduced.
use_when: The content was pulled, derived, or assembled elsewhere, and a reader may need to get back to the thing behind it.
instead_of: origin, method, reproduce, source_name, derived_from, built_by, acquired, transform, recorded_or_computed, trust_citation

gloss: What keeps this row true, and who or what does it.
use_when: The row can go stale, and the answer to 'what would catch that' is worth carrying beside it. Empty is an honest answer and says nothing holds it.

gloss: What is unresolved about this row, and who or what has to resolve it.
use_when: The row is not finished and the remainder is a live question. A unit of work belongs in the tracker; this is the loose end that has to travel with the row.
instead_of: question, awaiting, next, work, todo, pending

gloss: Anything about this row with no more specific home. The deliberate catch-all.
use_when: None of the others fits and forcing one would misdescribe the text. A `note` column doing two jobs wants to be two columns.
instead_of: notes, comment, remark, misc, aside, realized_outbien_note

gloss: Verbatim text from a source document, carried into the row unchanged.
use_when: The words are somebody else's and the row's value is that they are exact. The file should usually also be `supplied` in the content registry.
